$comment: Every refusal string in the ecosystem, in one place. A refusal that can be printed is a refusal that can be tested — and one registry makes them countable, localisable, and comparable across services. A consumer can render a meaningful message for a refusal from any service without knowing that service.

refusals.meaning: The access token is past its expiry. Revocation latency is bounded by this lifetime.
The token signature did not verify, or the token is malformed.
Participation is by facility and seat, never by person. A person without a seat cannot participate.
The tool has no classification. `unclassified` is a real value, not an absence — and defaulting a classification is not a fix, because the classification is a judgement about what the tool is for.
High-risk technical, clinical, structural, fire or hazardous-material content awaiting a qualified reviewer's signature. Readable and clearly labelled; not executable.
An approved version can never be edited. A change creates a new version and preserves the prior one.
Separation covers anybody who EDITED the version, not merely its recorded author — the stricter reading, and the correct one.
Required provenance metadata is missing. Provenance is per item, not per document.
Having a file does not imply permission to publish it. Publication requires confirmed or not-required permission.
The reviewer authored or edited this version.
Same rule, applied to transfer artifacts from Chapter 4 onward.
Reading is not doing. Refused at every named point, and asserted as an absence.
A corrective action is a commitment, not an accomplishment. Asserted twice, as an absence.
Only approved catalogue content earns. No progression tier may depend on content whose approval is pending.
A privacy position, not an omission. It costs support capability, and that cost is accepted deliberately.

Canon prohibits a formal assessment or transfer artifact in Chapters 1-3. An observation record has no review field to set — the absence is asserted on the shape, not enforced by a rule that could later be relaxed.
The external assertion's facility hint matched no claimed facility.
A NORMAL STATE, not an error. An unmatched facility queues an approval request rather than auto-creating a tenant — auto-creation would let anyone with an external account create one.

The adapter's subject identifier is not stable and opaque. An email is not stable; a display name is not opaque. Keying on either means a person who changes it becomes a new person, losing their standing and their seat.
Too many attempts. Rate limiting is present from R0 — the prior attempt had none anywhere, and credentials were attackable at full speed for fourteen releases.
Too many requests.
That state change is not in the transition table. canTransition is the only way to move; there is no direct state assignment.
A deprecated version is frozen. nextStates(deprecated) returns nothing.
The state is not in the machine at all — a data defect, not a client error.
Withdrawn content stays readable for the record and cannot be run as an instrument. Honoured before content is served, including offline.
Cached high-risk content is past its expiry and connectivity has not confirmed it is still current. General content warns and continues; high-risk stops. Enforcement mechanism E14.
Adapting class A or B content produces class C. A facility that edits official guidance and keeps the class A label has created content claiming an authority it no longer has.
